Precisely because it might not be safe either Relationships between people will be restructured People's social relationships will be restructured And what about the relationship between people and goods? That will be restructured too I think Alibaba faces the same challenge In the face of this giant wave which giants are safe? The challenge is enormous Looking at history is there any precedent? Companies from one era transitioning into the next era and still doing exceptionally well— are there many? It's not a question of how many It's a question of whether there are any at all Any at all? Basically none So this doesn't depend on your strategic choices No matter what, it's hard to stay at the table That's the despairing part That's not despairing at all People are born, age, get sick, and die 2:56 Companies also are born, age, decline, and die Nothing is more natural than that That's why new companies get their chance That's why young people can have dreams Professor Zeng, I've heard many entrepreneurs mention you They say a very important strategic transformation they made They say a very important strategic transformation they made may have come from taking your class at Hupan University There are many business school professors I wonder why so many entrepreneurs say they've been influenced by you What do you think makes you different from other business school professors? First of all, I think I was extremely lucky The Brutal Truth About the Laws of Business —— 来自商业规律的残酷真相 3:28 I had the opportunity to join Alibaba when the internet was growing fastest And I took part in a phase of hypergrowth for a company So that experience combined with my solid academic training allowed me to integrate theory with practice 3:46 Because while I was doing the work, I often thought about which of the things I used to teach could actually be applied And in the process I would also distill what new things could be turned into a theoretical framework that could still be used in the future So combining theory and practice was a major breakthrough And second, I have continuously studied frontier industry development 4:10 So when I talk with entrepreneurs besides discussing strategic methodology with them I can also explore with them how the industry will actually develop next and what kind of strategic decisions might be more appropriate So combining these two is a fairly rare capability Take Alibaba as an example Because this is the company you were personally involved with the longest Because this is the company you were personally involved with the longest Because this is the company you were personally involved with the longest Over the past 20 years, were there strategic decisions that truly determined Alibaba's survival? 4:37 Which ones would they be? I happen to be doing a retrospective lately So I'm quite familiar with Alibaba's first 15 years Because I participated in it fully In fact, the most important decisions were probably three Founding Taobao Founding Alipay Founding Alibaba Cloud And these three decisions were not only unrecognized by society at the time 5:00 The controversy inside the company was also extremely intense People may already know a lot about the controversy over Alibaba Cloud But when Taobao announced its founding several executives were very strongly opposed 5:16 Why? They felt Alibaba's original business hadn't matured yet And then you went to attack eBay's core main business And then you went to attack eBay's core main business The risk was too great So these are the three most important decisions Then there were the slightly less important ones Like how Taobao went from a platform for buying and selling goods to becoming an ecosystem supporting the development of e-commerce 5:39 And then how to go all in on mobile I think these two decisions were actually very important too But perhaps not as significant But as I just said, I should add one more point After you make a strategy there are still layer upon layer of decisions Secondary strategic decisions are also very important For example, in Alibaba Cloud's early days do you serve only one scenario or should the architecture support multiple service scenarios from the start? Should the scenario you serve be Taobao or search? 6:11 And open source or closed source? These were all second-level strategic questions with huge debate And further down, your database changed Should you build your own database? Then computing also changed And storage changed too That's how the slogan "de-IOE" came about back then That is, replacing IBM, Oracle, and EMC (storage) 6:35 So just like today, once computing is solved you find storage becomes the new bottleneck So in the process from strategy to execution there are many very important decisions The further down you go, the more strategy and tactics are tightly intertwined So making one big strategic decision isn't enough From decision to execution to finally seeing results 7:00 there is an enormous challenge At the moment of making a strategic decision how did you know it was a good strategy? Because there was so much controversy at the time Generally, because you make many strategies how do you judge that it is a good strategy? We didn't know Because we believed, we saw it All the truly great companies that became era-defining 7:21 were eventually proven right in their contrarian view Mm Of course, in the process there were also many crazy ideas that simply disappeared This point must be emphasized It's not crazy ideas What we see is the so-called survival bias You are seeing the bias of the winners 7:38 The most successful companies are necessarily contrarian But being contrarian doesn't guarantee success But at the time based on our own capabilities what we could see and were willing to believe in was that picture So strategy, to a large extent is actually about how to create the future It's not simply a plan Can only contrarian strategies achieve great success? 8:03 Can a consensus strategy achieve great success? I'm in a consensus track But I do it better than everyone else Can that achieve great success? That's excellence That's excellence Not greatness Yes Greatness must come from being contrarian Yes Now, in today's AI era we have entered a brand-new cyclical paradigm phase As you said, this is a new civilization Do you feel lost or anxious? As someone like you who formulates strategy when you look at the future how do you feel at a moment like this? 8:30 It is indeed very confusing Because you know many new things will certainly appear Because you know many new things will certainly appear But you don't know which are fleeting little ripples and which are the big waves representing the future What will change and what won't This is extremely confusing Which do you now see as small ripples and which as big waves? Do you have some preliminary thoughts and judgments?
